title: Trump Threatens to Fire Aides After Trip to Pro-Russian Territory
seoTitle: Trump Threatens Aides After Pro-Russian Territory Trip
subtitle: The decision comes after a report revealed paid work in Bosnia
excerpt: Donald Trump threatened to fire Chris LaCivita and James Blair if a conflict of interest is found, following their revealed trip to Republika Srpska for paid.
author: Daniele Morais
trending: chris lacivita james blair outside work
contentHtml:
Donald Trump announced he might dismiss two of his top political advisors if he discovers a conflict of interest related to external work. The measure was prompted by a report revealing that Chris LaCivita and James Blair traveled to Republika Srpska, a territory in Bosnia-Herzegovina aligned with Russia, to provide paid consultancy.

LaCivita and Blair's Trip and Payment

According to The New York Times, LaCivita, co-campaign manager for Trump's 2024 campaign, and Blair, former deputy chief of staff who leads the MAGA Inc. super PAC, went to Republika Srpska last week. They reportedly received “hundreds of thousands of dollars each” through a Washington law firm hired by the region's government to advise on electoral matters.

Trump's Stance on External Consultants

In a post on Truth Social, Trump declared that LaCivita and Blair are “external consultants” who do not work directly for him, except as advisors. He further stated that if there is a conflict of interest, “I will fire them immediately.” The president emphasized that he is unaware of the advisors' other clients but intends to question them.

Advisors' Relationship with Trump's Campaign

Blair continues to lead the MAGA Inc. super PAC, responsible for coordinating Trump's strategy in the midterm elections. LaCivita, in turn, serves as a senior advisor for the same super PAC. Both have been central figures in efforts to bolster Republican candidates in traditionally conservative districts that now show vulnerability in polls.

Context of the Midterm Elections

The trips occurred shortly before the elections in Republika Srpska, scheduled for Sunday, and coincide with polls indicating significant challenges for Republicans in the United States. The involvement of high-ranking advisors in external work raises questions about resource allocation and potential conflicts with the national campaign's objectives.

Press Reaction and Potential Consequences

The revelations generated coverage in international media, including CNN and The Guardian, which highlighted the possibility of dismissals and the need for clarification from the advisors. As of now, there are no indications that LaCivita or Blair have publicly responded to the conflict of interest accusations.

With information from CNN, The Guardian.
